# Udāyittheragāthā (Thag 15.2)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Udāyittheragāthā* (Thag 15.2) is a poetic discourse attributed to the elder Udāyi, located within the fifteenth chapter (verses of sixteen stanzas) of the *Theragāthā* in the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations of the text include an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato, with ten translations across nine languages recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

The text shares an extensive parallel relationship with the *Nāgasutta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 6.43) [SuttaCentral]. This textual overlap is corroborated by DharmaNexus, which matches verses §0.4–16.5 of the *Udāyittheragāthā* with AN 6.43 (§43.5.1–43.20.4) at a 0.96 similarity score [DharmaNexus]. The text is also extensively quoted and commented upon in the second volume of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Beyond the Pali canon, SuttaCentral lists a curated passage-level parallel in the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 118, 龍象) and notes a resembling parallel in the Jain *Uttarādhyayanasūtra* 25 [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus independently confirms cross-language alignment with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) and additionally detects verse alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* (D4094) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
